items.text: The software shall supervise the tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, each released every 10 ms in that order, and the task T_DIAG, released after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period, using the task set, periods and release order given by the configuration data.

The software shall read the set of supervised tasks, their periods, their start limits, their execution limits and their release order from the configuration data block, so that a change of these values requires no change of the software code.

The software shall start alive supervision only after the code integrity check and the configuration integrity check at start-up have both passed and the configuration values have been found within their allowed ranges.
items.rationale: The system requirement names the start-up integrity checks; the range check of SYS-SUP-010 is a start-up check on the same data and is included so that supervision never runs on out-of-range values.

items.text: When no completion notification of a supervised task has been received for 2 consecutive periods of that task, the software shall detect an alive fault (fault code 1) for that task at the end of the second period.

When no start notification of a supervised task has been received by the end of its start limit (default 2 ms after its release), the software shall detect a late start (fault code 2) for that task no later than 100 µs after the end of the start limit; a start notification received at a start delay equal to the start limit, or earlier, is within the limit and is not a late start.

When no completion notification of a supervised task has been received by the end of its execution limit (default 3 ms for T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, 20 ms for T_DIAG, counted from its start notification), the software shall detect an overrun (fault code 3) for that task no later than 100 µs after the end of the execution limit; a completion notification received at an execution time equal to the execution limit, or earlier, is within the limit and is not an overrun.
The software shall measure start delays and execution times of supervised tasks from a time base of 100 µs resolution.
The software shall treat a measured start delay or execution time equal to its limit as within the limit.

At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoint notifications of the tasks released in that cycle have not been received in the configured release order or one of them is missing, the software shall detect a program flow fault (fault code 4).

When a program flow fault is detected, the software shall report as entity the task expected at the first position where the received checkpoint notifications, compared position by position with the configured release order, differ or are missing.
When a program flow fault is detected, the software shall make one fault report per control cycle.

At start-up, when a configuration value is outside its allowed range (a timing limit longer than the period of its task, a zero period or an unknown task), the software shall detect a configuration fault (fault code 9, entity CONFIG).
At start-up, when a configuration fault (fault code 9) has been detected, the software shall not start alive supervision.
The software shall accept from each supervised task, for each release, a start notification, a checkpoint notification and a completion notification.
items.rationale: The system requirements speak of tasks starting, completing and arriving checkpoints but do not define what the software receives. This item fixes the software inputs from which the supervision decisions are made. Whether the checkpoint coincides with the start or the completion notification is left to sw-arch (OP-SWR-002).

items.text: The software shall accept the release instants of the supervised tasks from the timer-driven scheduler.
items.rationale: Split from SWR-SUP-011: the system requirements speak of task releases but do not define what the software receives. This item fixes the release-instant input from which start delays and periods are measured.

items.text: At start-up, the software shall configure the independent watchdog with a timeout of 100 ms, clocked independently of the main clock.
At start-up, the software shall configure the window watchdog so that a refresh earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh causes a reset.
While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected, the software shall refresh the window watchdog once per control cycle, at the end of the control cycle.
While every supervised task is healthy and no fault has been detected, the software shall service the independent watchdog at least once within every 100 ms timeout period.

When a fault is detected, except a watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) that does not latch the safe state, the software shall stop servicing both watchdogs, without exception, until the next reset.

When a watchdog reset occurs before the fault report and the safe-state entry of the fault being handled have completed, the software shall, as the first start-up step after the reset and before any other start-up step, configure both control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low, and keep them low until the start-up integrity checks have passed, after which the signals are governed by SWR-SAFE-005 and SWR-SAFE-020 for the status signal and by the safe-state requirements for the control outputs.
items.rationale: End condition aligned with SWR-SAFE-003 (low until the start-up integrity checks have passed): it does not conflict with SWR-SAFE-005, which drives the status signal high only after those checks pass, with no fault detected and the latch clear, and with SWR-SAFE-016, which lets start-up continue after a code 8 report that does not latch the safe state. Software obligation starts at the point where software can configure the pins. The interval from reset until that configuration is allocated to the board (external pull-down resistors holding the signals low, pins as inputs) by SYS-PLAT-002 per CON-SUP-132, and is not a software obligation.

items.text: When the third detection of fault code 8 latches the safe state, the software shall stop servicing both watchdogs until the next reset.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-WDG-007 at software level: a code 8 detection that sets the latch is a safe-state entry and servicing stops.

items.text: When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) and it is not the third detection of fault code 8 that latches the safe state, the software shall continue to service both watchdogs as in any start-up.

At start-up, before any supervised task is released, the software shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the program code from linker symbol __app_start to __app_end, processing the bytes in increasing address order, and compare it with the little-endian reference word of four bytes stored at linker symbol __app_crc.

At start-up, before any supervised task is released, the software shall compute the CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR) over the configuration data block, processing the bytes in increasing address order, and compare it with the CRC-32 stored with that block as a little-endian reference word of four bytes.

When the CRC-32 of the program code at start-up differs from its reference, the software shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up (fault code 5, entity CODE) at the completion of the computation.

When the CRC-32 of the configuration data block differs from its stored value, the software shall detect a configuration integrity fault (fault code 6, entity CONFIG) at the completion of the computation.
While supervising, the software shall process one 1 KiB segment of the program code with the run-time code check in every control cycle.
The software shall complete a full run-time code check pass over a 1 MiB program image within 11 s.
items.rationale: One 1 KiB segment per 10 ms control cycle (SWR-MEM-005) gives 1024 segments in 10.24 s for a 1 MiB image, which is within the limit.

items.text: The software shall limit the processor time used by the run-time code check to 0.5 ms per control cycle.

When the run-time code check finds a mismatch with the reference CRC-32, the software shall detect a code integrity fault at run time (fault code 7, entity CODE) at the completion of the failing integrity computation.

When a fault is detected, except a watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) that does not latch the safe state, the software shall enter the safe state by driving both control outputs low and the status signal low.
items.rationale: Software share of the 50 ms safe-state limit of SYS-SAFE-001: 49 ms (SWR-SAFE-002), on the assumption of CON-SUP-133 that the board output stage takes at most 1 ms from the pin change to the output level.

items.text: When a fault is detected, except a watchdog reset reported at start-up (fault code 8) that does not latch the safe state, the software shall have changed the control output pins and the status signal pin to low within 49 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
From the start of start-up after any reset until the start-up integrity checks have passed, the software shall keep both control outputs and the status signal low.
After a reset, the software shall configure the two control outputs and the status signal as outputs driven low before any other start-up step.

When the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault has been detected since the latest reset and the safe-state latch is clear, the software shall drive the status signal high to show that the controller is operational. A watchdog reset report at start-up (fault code 8) is not a fault detection for this condition, whether or not it is the first, second or third report of fault code 8; it counts only toward the latch rule of SWR-SAFE-007.
items.rationale: The operational indication is conditional on the safe-state latch being clear, consistent with SWR-SAFE-007, SWR-SAFE-009 and SWR-SAFE-010. A code 8 report records a reset that already happened and is not a fault detection (CON-SUP-137, CON-SUP-130), so it neither prevents the status signal from going high nor overrides the latch condition; a third report latches the safe state under SWR-SAFE-007 and SWR-SAFE-011, and the latch-clear condition then fails (SWR-SAFE-020). Split from the former combined requirement; the latch-set case is SWR-SAFE-020.

items.text: While the safe-state latch is set, including a latch retained across a watchdog reset, the software shall keep the status signal low.
items.rationale: Split from SWR-SAFE-005 to keep one shall per requirement.

items.text: When the software enters the safe state at a detection that is the first or the second of its fault code, other than fault code 9, the software shall request a software reset within 20 ms after the later of the completion of the fault report and the completion of the safe-state entry.
When the per-code count of detections of a fault code reaches three, the software shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.

The software shall count toward the 60 s of fault-free operation only time spent in the OPERATIONAL state, with an under-count of at most 10 ms per reset and at most 100 µs per update, and never an over-count.
The software shall keep the latch, the fault history, the fault count and the per-code detection counts across software resets and watchdog resets.
When a configuration fault is detected at start-up, the software shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8), the software shall count it as a detection of fault code 8 for the latch rule of SWR-SAFE-007.
While the safe state is latched after the third detection of the same fault code, the software shall not request a software reset.
At a loss of power, the software shall lose the latch, the fault history, the fault count and the per-code detection counts, each count starting at zero after the power-on reset.
While the safe state is latched after a configuration fault (fault code 9) at start-up, the software shall not request a software reset.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-SAFE-014 at software level: the reset rule excludes fault code 9.

items.text: When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) as the first or the second detection of fault code 8, the software shall not request a software reset because of that report.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-SAFE-015 at software level.

items.text: When a watchdog reset is reported at start-up (fault code 8) and it is not the third detection of fault code 8 without 60 s of fault-free operation since the first, the software shall continue start-up without entering the safe state by this report alone.
The software shall keep a separate count of detections for each fault code, a detection of a different fault code neither resetting nor advancing it.

When 60 s of fault-free operation, counted within the bounds of SWR-SAFE-008, have been reached since the latest fault detection, the software shall return the count of each fault code to zero at that point and at no earlier point.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-SAFE-018 at software level.

items.text: When a fault is detected, the software shall restart the accumulation of the 60 s of fault-free operation at zero, so that only time counted under SWR-SAFE-008 after the latest fault detection, including across resets, is accumulated and time counted before a detection is never added to time counted after it.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-SAFE-019 at software level.

items.text: At start-up, the software shall read the reset flags and classify the cause of the latest reset as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor (software) reset or other.
After classifying the reset cause, the software shall send the reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: Answers OP-SYS-001 (deferred to sw-req) only in part: the inputs still do not define the text format and terminator of the start-up message, so it is raised again as OP-SWR-001. The requirement is verifiable as written (a message carrying the cause is sent after classification).

items.text: When the classified reset cause is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the software shall report a watchdog reset fault (fault code 8) with the entity IWDG or WWDG, the watchdog whose reset flag was set.
The software shall configure the diagnostic serial line for 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

When a fault is detected, or when the watchdog reset fault (fault code 8) is reported under SWR-RST-003, except when a watchdog reset occurs before the transmission has completed, the software shall transmit on the diagnostic serial line a fault report in the form FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed, this form applying also to the fault code 8 report, with the codes 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset and 9 configuration out of range.

When a fault is detected, the software shall complete the transmission of the fault report within 10 ms of the detection, except when a watchdog reset occurs before the transmission has completed, in which case no report is required for the fault that was being handled.
The software shall use as entity of a fault report the name of the affected task for the fault codes 1, 2 and 3, CODE for the fault codes 5 and 7, and CONFIG for the fault codes 6 and 9.

The software shall give as <ms since start> in a fault report for the fault codes other than the watchdog reset fault the time of detection of the fault, counted in milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, as an unsigned decimal number representable in four bytes that wraps to zero after 4294967295 ms.
items.rationale: Scoped to codes other than 8 because a code 8 report at start-up records a reset that already happened and is not a fault detection (CON-SUP-137); the inputs define no timestamp event for it. Raised as OP-SWR-003.

items.text: When the service request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic serial line, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall answer STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SWR-DIAG-016.

The software shall report as <state> STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks pass, OPERATIONAL while supervising with no fault, SAFE from the instant a fault is detected, during start-up or operation, until the next reset, a code 8 report at start-up alone not being such a detection and leaving the reported state STARTUP, and LATCHED while the latch is set, LATCHED overriding the other states.
The software shall give as <fault count> the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset.

When the service request GET FAULTS is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall answer within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SWR-DIAG-016, with the most recent eight fault reports, or all fault reports when fewer than eight exist, oldest first, one per line, followed by a line END, or only END when none exists.

When the service request GET RESET is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall answer RST,<cause> within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SWR-DIAG-016, with <cause> given as POR for power-on, IWDG for independent watchdog, WWDG for window watchdog, SW for supervisor (software) reset and OTHER for other, according to the classification of SWR-RST-001.

When any other service request is received, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall answer ERR within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of the request to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SWR-DIAG-016.

When a fault report is made while eight fault reports are held, the software shall discard the oldest held fault report and hold the new one, so that the eight most recent fault reports since the last power-on reset are held.
items.rationale: Mirrors the derived split SYS-DIAG-012 at software level: the fault history is a bounded store of eight reports.

items.text: The software shall accept a service request on the diagnostic serial line as a line of at most 32 ASCII characters ended by a line feed, the request being received when its line feed is received.

When a line longer than 32 characters is received on the diagnostic serial line, other than while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall answer ERR within 50 ms, counted from the receipt of its line feed to the end of the last character of the answer, the 50 ms being extended as stated in SWR-DIAG-016.
When a service request, or a line longer than 32 characters, is received while the answer to an earlier service request is still being transmitted, the software shall discard it without answering it.

When fault reports are transmitted between the receipt of a service request and the end of its answer, the software shall extend the 50 ms answer time of that request by the transmission time of those fault reports.
When a fault report and the answer to a service request are both waiting for transmission on the diagnostic serial line, the software shall transmit the fault report first.

In normal operation (no fault, no service request), the software shall limit the supervisor execution time to 10 % of the processor time over any 1 s window, measured on the simulator at the configured core clock.
The supervisor software shall be written in C11 without dynamic memory allocation and without recursion.
The software shall build and run on the Renode simulator with STM32N6 platform descriptions, without the real board.
In test builds, the software shall provide a test hook that injects each fault class (fault codes 1 to 9).
In builds other than test builds, the software shall not contain the fault injection test hooks.

open_points.text: The text format and terminator of the start-up message that carries the reset cause (SWR-RST-002) are not defined by the inputs (CON-SUP-111 says only that the cause is sent). Raised again from OP-SYS-001. The requirement is correct and verifiable without the answer; the message framing is a detail for the design.

The inputs do not say whether the checkpoint notification of a task coincides with its start notification or its completion notification (SWR-SUP-011, SWR-SUP-008). The software requirements are correct as written with three named notifications; the mapping is an architecture decision.

No product decision defines the <ms since start> value of a code 8 report. CON-SUP-137 says the report records a reset that already happened and is not a fault detection, so 'time of detection' (SWR-DIAG-005) has no clear event for it. A person must decide the timestamp event for code 8 (for example the instant the report is generated, or a fixed value) and add it to the product decisions; SWR-DIAG-005 is scoped to the other codes until then.
